newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Lagardere makes Thomson-CSF bid.
newsitem.headline: France's Lagardere makes Thomson-CSF bid.

text.p: French conglomerate Lagardere said it filed its bid on Wednesday for defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF.
It had the necessary finances for the acquisition and an eventual public offer to buy out Thomson-CSF's minority shareholders if its bid succeeded.
It has cash, bank credit lines and would issue a five billion franc ($859.5 million) bond convertible into Thomson-CSF shares, Lagardere said in a statement.
The bond would be a one-year, eurofranc issue and is underwritten by Credit Lyonnais and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
It will be repaid in cash and Thomson-CSF shares depending on terms of a planned merger between Thomson-CSF and Matra High Tecnhologies and the public offer to Thomson-CSF minorities.

Lagardere is in this way committing itself to repaying the bond in Thomson-CSF shares at a fixed price which may be lower than that it will pay for Thomson-CSF stock in its public offer to minorities.

But "the risk should not be significant in view of the size of the expected investment," it said. The bond will be issued in the days following the government's decision. The selling price to investors does not prejudice the price of Lagardere's bid for Thomson-CSF.
The offer to minorities will be led by Banque Nationale de Paris. BNP is also providing Lagardere with a credit line for the Thomson-CSF transactions, it said.

Separately, Alcatel Alsthom said it has made its firm offer for Thomson, while General Electric Co Plc said it has memoranda of understanding with both Alcatel and Lagardere in their bids. ($ = 5.817 French Francs)
